item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q018_tal_effector_repeat_lengths","answer":"SCOPe assigns d2kq5a_, d3v6pa_, and d4cj9a_ to a.298.1.1 because all three contain the homologous TAL-effector repeat unit and its characteristic all-alpha, tandemly repeated superhelical architecture. d2kq5a_ is a short repeat fragment, whereas d3v6pa_ and d4cj9a_ contain longer arrays or differently bounded constructs. TAL arrays expand and contract through changes in the number of roughly 34-residue repeats, so total chain length is not a family-defining feature. The family-level homology is strongest between corresponding repeat modules; it does not require a reliable end-to-end alignment of the complete, unequal-length arrays. Likewise, family membership supports transfer of the repeat scaffold and general DNA-recognition mechanism, but not DNA-target specificity: specificity depends chiefly on each repeat's repeat-variable diresidue and on repeat order and array length. Short fragments are therefore useful structural templates for local repeat geometry but not automatically for whole-array curvature, full-length effector behavior, or target prediction. Representative selection should account for repeat count, construct boundaries, RVD composition, and DNA-bound state rather than treating the longest chain as universally representative.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
